marketingRemarks.marketingRemark: Welcome to an extraordinary residence in the highly sought-after gated HOA community of Camelot Estates in Merced. Built in 2023, this meticulously maintained 4-bedroom, 3-bath home showcases exceptional upgrades, premium features, and thoughtful design throughout, offering the perfect blend of luxury, comfort, efficiency, and modern living. The home features an owned solar system providing long-term energy savings with no leased equipment, a whole-house water filtration system, a whole-house fan for added comfort and efficiency, and custom plantation shutters throughout for enhanced privacy, style, and energy efficiency. Additional concrete improvements in both the front and backyard provide enhanced functionality, accessibility, and low-maintenance outdoor living. Smart home and security features include a Ring video doorbell, security cameras, exterior security lighting, and strategically placed outdoor speakers for an elevated living experience. The true centerpiece of this remarkable property is the resort-inspired backyard, designed for unforgettable entertaining. Enjoy a custom gas-heated swimming pool with an integrated spa, cascading waterfalls, and custom fire features creating a private oasis right at home. The outdoor space has been thoughtfully designed for future expansion with pre-installed gas, electrical, and water connections ready for an outdoor kitchen, additional entertainment areas, landscaping, and more. A pre-plumbed outdoor bathroom area with connections for a shower, sink, and toilet adds even more possibilities for future customization. Located in one of Merced's most desirable and exclusive communities, Camelot Estates offers a premier lifestyle with luxury, privacy, and convenience. This rare opportunity delivers the upgrades, amenities, and resort-style living that discerning buyers have been waiting for.

Donn B. Chenoweth is by far one of the best schools I've ever attended. The teachers are wonderful, all of the staff is very kind. they've created a one of a kind learning environment. The kids are not awarded for average performance, but for their achievements. They hold assemblies where some get responsibilty, caring, trustworthiness, honesty, respect, or citizenship. these categories are known as the six pillars.They also may get awards for accelerated reader, mathematical achievements, or for successfully learning english on top of their native language. I truly apprieciate what this school has done for all of the students, and I feel bad because they are extremely low on their budget and they've had to cut some field trips and other things they do annually for the students. But overall, they deserve two thumbs up!

schoolReviews.review: My eldest child went through this school and my youngest is currently enrolled now. I immediately must warn you….BEWARE of the assistant principal! She will speak over you if you have a concern and make matters MUCH worse. She’s a nightmare. I definitely recommend skipping her and going straight to the head Principal for your concern. He definitely takes care of business and will treat you with respect. Unfortunately this school has A LOT of kid drama. Just in this past 2 weeks there have been 6-8 fights. It got so bad that our kids called us to pick them up cause they were scared. I pulled up to a long line out the door of upset parents waiting to sign their kid out after lunch. School never called to let us know what was going on. It’s just absurd. When it comes to teaching, some teachers can be helpful and some are obviously there to get a paycheck. They don’t care. Don’t believe me… go check out the schools math rating. Last time I checked the percentage of students achieving proficiency in math is 29% (which is lower than the California state average of 40%). At what point are we not going to start blaming the teachers for this insane percentage? My youngest kid’s math teacher will not accept ANY late HW even if sick. I have a ton of college classes under my belt (100 units plus) and I’ve never encountered a teacher like this one. During the student teacher meeting, she either looked at me with a blank stare or just repeatedly said no with a smirk when I asked her if there was anything my kid could do to make up for it. I could go on and on about it but I’ll just leave you with this reminder….. there is a reason this school has a 3/10 rating. Can not wait till my kid is done with this school. Good luck to all you other parents and just pray your child can get through this school without feeling mentally beaten down.

I find the staff rude and often passive aggressive with students. That excludes the teachers though, or at least some. I find my teachers very nice, helpful, and caring although there is that one or two teachers at this school that I can describe more negatively. I feel like the way they solve problems at this school is not OK. They don't even bother to alert parents either most of the time when there's a student issue. Their dress code is ridiculous as well. They can dress code you for wearing red then put you in all blue. The overall learning and friends experience comes down to the student though. If your child or student wants to learn they will. The teachers provide sufficient help and guidance to make sure you can pass the grade. It's just up to the student to pay attention and the amount of motivation they have. One thing though is there is a lot of student drama. It can be fights or student encounters and just people who don't like each other. But there are ways you can avoid that and if you have a problem you can just go up to the office and they handle it. They can also have absurd rules, for example once you leave the field during lunch you can't go back on campus which I've tried to imagine why they would do that but i can't, it makes no sense. If it wasn't for my friends all being at Hoover, I would definitely switch schools.

I was put in detention for no reason after being called names and being cussed at. Supposedly I used "Profanity" against the kids cussing and calling ME names. I highly recommend to listen to your kid if they say they are being bullied at school and try to do something about it.

I have found the entire staff of this school to be exceptional team players in a cohesive effort to educate and enrich the lives and education of students in their program. They show genuine regard and respect for each and every student and parent in the program; as well as staff and auxilliary staff members. It has been my experience that, this team of exceptional educators, administrators, and classified staff, put out 150% personal and professional effort in the course of each and every day.

I have horrible experience with this school. Beware. My son don't want to go to this school. And the 6th grader teacher always picky and put my son on detention all the time. I can tell you more about how horrible my experience in this Cruikshank Middle School.

I like that it is the type of school where most students know each other from their younger days and yet, they have been welcoming to students like mine, who are transplants. Parents seem to be engaged, FFA seems great and there are lots of programs, clubs and pathways for students to explore.

This is an amazing campus to work at. I feel supported by both administration and parents, which is not always the case at other schools. I have some of the best kids in the district in my classes and for the most part, they all work hard and do their best. This is a wonderful school!!!

schoolReviews.review: This school has been a good school for my children. It IS the teachers that make this school a good school. I would have rated this school higher but when my 3rd grader started struggling in his class, I started asking him what was wrong at first he wouldn't tell me. But after he started leaving his classroom crying enough was enough. He was not that he was misbehaving. It was because he was stressed. He even told the principal this ( WITHOUT ME THERE) Even after having a meeting with his teacher things still did not change. I also found out that there were other children transfered to another class. I just felt like the principal is not taking these situations seriously. I had to teach my 9 yr old child that just because one person doesn't make him feel special does not mean it's true.CHILDREN ARE LIKE FLOWERS...IF YOU STEP ON THEM THEY WILL NEVER GROW.

The school, staff and teachers are to commended. My children have attended Peterson since they were in Kindergarten, my youngest daughter will be moving on to middle school this next year, so we will be leaving Peterson. I cannot say enough great things about all the teachers, especially Ms. Parker this year, the entire school staff, nor will I ever be able to thank them for the love, care and commitment they provided. What a great experience... Thank you so very much Peterson staff!
Wonderful teacher parent evolvement, this school care for the students and does everything to make sure they are all getting a good education.

This school is the best. The staff is wonderful. They all are friendly and listen to each parent. The principal, Mr. Harris, does a wonderful job. He is always outside and about on the campus greeting parents and watching over the children. If there is ever any concern he makes sure to address it imediatley. Parents are very involved and all around the children love coming to school.

schoolReviews.review: This has been a wonderful school for my 2 daughters! Loving teachers and a challenging curriculum, all in a Christ-Centered environment! Love PCS!
We are extremely happy with their pre school program. Our daughter is thriving. She will be well prepared for kindergarten. They are so loving and preparing her well with a solid foundation.

My children are enrolled at PCS as i type this. Im very disappointed at how this school is ran. After the school year i will be taking my children out. I like that have they Chapel i cant complain about that but everything else isn't so good from my experience.

The teachers, staff and parents here are a blessing many going above and beyond what is expected of them. I currently have children in the elementary grades and I couldn't be more happy with the education. But I must say it's mostly the love and care in which they handle each situation, that gives me the most comfort in leaving my children in their care. Providence Christian School is truly Gods school.

Providence Christian is has been a wonderful fit for our child. This is his second year there (currently a 6th grade student). I was worried about his transition to Jr. High but I need not have done so. The staff, teachers and principal have made it very easy! We get a lot of one-on-one attention, easy and accessible communication and I know I am always welcome on campus. I would recommend PCS to ANY parent looking for a private Christian school!
PCS has been a wonderful place for my children to learn in a Godly environment.

Providence offers high quality Christian education. I have twins in the junior high and LOVE what they are doing. the teachers care and challenge them. They both played sports and are growing in a safe environment.

This school is amazing. Definitely has some of the best teachers you can find. Mr. Abejuela has a pull-up bar in his classroom and challenges students not only mentally but physically. Mr. Dissalvo always presents both sides to any argument so we could form our own opinions and even let us debate in the middle of class often. Mr. Wendel wrote a song and sang it with his guitar for our class at the end of the year, it was hilarious! Mr. Graham was an amazing science teacher and made learning about moles and the periodic table interesting. Ms. Alvarez was the most passionate teacher who ensured that each and every student had the help they needed to pass her class. Finally, Mr. Rivero always had a smile on his face and being in his class, even during Saturday school, brought happiness.

Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Merced High School and graduated in 2011. I was able to experience a variety of great teachers and learned skills I wasn't aware some schools don't have as a standard. They prepare students for jobs with mock interviews, resumes, cover letters and we covered a course on how to get into stocks. There was cooking and a home living elective class as well as many others. The school was also available to special need students and even though their classes were separate, they encouraged us all to have healthy interactions with eachother. So we'd have rallies and special events together. Another good benefit to the student is that the school has an open campus policy that gave Juniors and Seniors privileges to leave the campus during lunch as an insentive and if your academics are poor then you'd get the privilege revoked. If you are doing poorly in school, we have great counselors who care about your academics as long as you show an interest in wanting to succeed. They are also attentive to last year students, so that they are all prepared to graduate or even move on to other career paths. I received all these benefits as a student before the new high school was built and there was about 30 student average per teacher, so I can only imagine how great of an education these students can get going to Merced High School now with the new gym being built and a much more breathable school environment.

This school is simple and a bit old compared to the nearby schools. It has some problems such as old rooms and such stuff but overall appearance wise this school is okay. I like how the original Merced High School is the best overall school wise in the county. This school could improve by having more school spirit and landscape. In the old days this school actually had flowers!

entryPointFlyout.value:
Wind Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wind Model, which forecasts how hurricanes and costs from resulting wind damages to structures will change over time due to climate change.

A property's Wind Factor indicates its likelihood to experience extreme winds over the next 30 years, from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Wind Factor scores are more likely to experience higher winds more frequently today and in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on the likelihood and speed of hurricane, tornado, or severe storm winds reaching this property, it has minimal wind risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's wind risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows this property's likelihood of being in a tropical storm event with 3-second wind gusts exceeding 50 mph (39 mph for 1-minute sustained winds) over the next 30 years.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all wind data on firststreet.org

expandableSummary.value: Estimated 22-32% chance of a flood reaching the building in the next 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Flood Factor® is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street Flood Model, a nationwide, probabilistic flood model that shows a location’s risk of flooding from rain, rivers, tides, and storm surge. It builds off of decades of peer-reviewed research and forecasts how flood risks will change over time due to changes in the environment. Flood Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of flood.

A property's Flood Factor is an indicator of its comprehensive flood risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Flood Factors are more likely to have flooded in the past, and are more likely to flood in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property’s projected likelihood and depth of flooding, it has major flood risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's flood risk is decreasing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Flood risk accumulates over time. Cumulative risk is calculated to the largest building or center of an empty lot. Raised or elevated buildings may not be as vulnerable as ground-level buildings or buildings with basements.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: This property has a 27% chance of flooding in the next 30 years.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all flood data on firststreet.org

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout.value:
The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable estimated zone.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is a government agency that maps flood zones in communities across the US, identifying areas of varying flood risk on Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). FEMA creates FIRMs to inform flood insurance pricing in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and to guide floodplain management regulations for NFIP-participating communities.

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout2.value: The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable zone as estimated by MassiveCert, Inc.

riskSpecificSubsectionDescription.value: This property is estimated to be in FEMA Zone X (unshaded), which is designated as a low-to-moderate risk flood area. In this zone, the risk of flooding is reduced, but not completely removed.

insuranceFlyout.value: To help you understand what it costs to protect this home with flood insurance we've partnered with Neptune Flood. Redfin may receive a commission if you purchase a policy through this link. There may be other flood insurance providers in your area.

insuranceDescription.value:

Flood insurance for this home ranges from $507 to $1088 per year, based on information from 6 providers.

expandableSummary.value: 9% chance of being in a wildfire in next 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Fire Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wildfire Model's nationwide, behavioral wildfire model that shows a specific location's probabilistic risk of wildfire based on the vegetation, topography, and fire weather in the surrounding area. Fire Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of fire.

A property's Fire Factor indicates its cumulative wildfire risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Fire Factors are more likely to be in a wildfire in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property's distance to wildfire risk areas and burnable vegetation, it has major wildfire risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's fire risk is increasing as weather patterns change.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Wildfire risk accumulates over time, so a property with a 0.1% chance of wildfire this year would have at least a 3% chance of being affected by wildfire at least once within 30 years. Being affected by wildfire refers to any actively burning fuels coming into contact with the largest building on the property.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: Within the next 30 years, this property has a 9% cumulative chance of being in a wildfire.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all fire data on firststreet.org

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout.value: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is a government agency that maps flood zones in communities across the US, identifying areas of varying flood risk on Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). FEMA creates FIRMs to inform flood insurance pricing in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and to guide floodplain management regulations for NFIP-participating communities.

riskSpecificSubsectionDescription.value: This property is located in a county with an average wildfire risk greater than 69.20% of counties in the United States.

insuranceFlyout.value: Most homeowners insurance typically includes fire coverage but in some areas, this will need to be purchased separately. Investing in fire insurance is one way to offset the cost of wildfire damage, and can help reduce your financial risk.

insuranceDescription.value: Fire insurance for this home ranges from $659 to $1223 per year, based on information from 7 providers.

expandableSummary.value: 7 days above 104° expected this year, 16 days in 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Heat Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. Heat Factor™ uses the First Street Extreme Heat Model to determine property-specific heat risk across the United States. The model is a spatial temperature model that determines a specific location’s exposure to extreme heat events based on the surface temperature, topography, land cover, and humidity in the surrounding area.

A property's Heat Factor indicates its risk of extreme heat exposure over the next thirty years, ranging from 1 (minimal risk) to 10 (extreme risk). Heat Factors are based on the current average daily high temperature and humidity of a property’s specific location during the hottest month of the year, and considers how it’s expected to grow over the next 30 years.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on current and future temperature and humidity in the area and at this specific location, this property has severe heat risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's heat risk is increasing as weather patterns change.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows the number of days exceeding what is considered a hot day at this property. This is defined by using the 98th percentile “feels like” temperature in this area, or the hottest 7 days in the 4km area surrounding this property for a given year and using the lowest “high” temperature from those 7 days as a base. A property may have more or less hot days than the surrounding area depending on its individual exposure to heat.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: A “hot day” in this area is considered to be any day with a “feels like” temperature of 104º. Over the next 30 years, this property is expected to see a 9% increase in the number of hot days per year.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all heat data on firststreet.org

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows the change in the number of poor air quality days over time, where the Air Quality Index (AQI) exceeds 100. These are the expected number of poor air quality days in a bad year, which is defined as a year with higher than average wildfire activity. This increases the amount of particulate matter (PM2.5) in the air and therefore worsens air quality.
